assets.content:
Subject: Analytics without cookies or trackers
Preview text: Review the installation path for one representative client website.

Give a suitable client site useful analytics

Hi there,

Give a suitable client website analytics without adding cookies, trackers or personal-data processing.

Simple Analytics is privacy-friendly website analytics designed around those conditions. No cookies or trackers are used, so visitor consent is not required for the analytics. Under GDPR, no DPA is required because Simple Analytics does not process personal data.

Installation is adapted to each website. During onboarding, Simple Analytics scans the site’s technology and provides corresponding HTML code, along with documented options for supported platforms and frameworks.

Enter onboarding with one representative website you have permission to assess. You can review its technology-specific installation option and decide whether the privacy design and setup path suit a client build.

Start for free → https://www.simpleanalytics.com/signup

- Simple Analytics

asset_metadata.single_idea: Simple Analytics can give a suitable client website useful analytics without cookies, trackers or personal-data processing, and its onboarding provides installation guidance based on that site's technology.

selected_brief.selection_reason: The audience research shows developers disputing whether privacy-friendly analytics actually avoids consent requirements. The product's documented absence of cookies, trackers and personal-data processing directly addresses that decision and is more broadly relevant than assuming the reader currently uses GA4.

value_case.reader_benefit: For a suitable client website, the developer can provide website analytics without adding cookies or trackers or processing visitors' personal data, reducing the analytics-related consent and DPA questions created by those practices.
value_case.mechanism: Simple Analytics states that it uses no cookies or trackers, requires no visitor consent and does not process personal data. During onboarding, it scans the website's technology and provides a corresponding installation option.
decision_conditions: The no-DPA statement rests on Simple Analytics' documented absence of personal-data processing and its stated GDPR basis; it is not a universal legal opinion for every client or jurisdiction.
Installation is per website and depends on the technology detected.
Client permission and suitability must be established before deployment.

claim_conditions: Describe the privacy benefit as Simple Analytics' documented product behavior, not a universal legal guarantee.
Keep the evaluation scoped to a representative website rather than an entire client portfolio.
Installation instructions vary with the website's detected technology.
Add each website and use the technology-detected HTML code or another documented platform or framework installation option.

The documented per-site installation and privacy behavior support an exploratory product evaluation across client builds, but R15 describes the additional-website rule in a subdomain context and does not establish the Self-serve site cap or aggregate portfolio cost; the research also does not verify firsthand agency demand or recipient qualification.
These sources document Simple Analytics' own behavior and stated GDPR basis; they do not establish a universal legal conclusion for every client configuration or jurisdiction.
selected_brief.target_audience: Agency or freelance developer choosing the analytics stack for client sites
selected_brief.job: Get the reader to consider Simple Analytics for a suitable client build and begin a scoped self-serve evaluation.
selected_brief.single_idea: Simple Analytics can give a suitable client website useful analytics without cookies, trackers or personal-data processing, and its onboarding provides installation guidance based on that site's technology.
selected_brief.felt_need: Whether adopting a cookie-free or 'privacy-friendly' analytics tool actually removes the need for a cookie consent banner is directly disputed among developers, with claims that named alternatives (Fathom, Plausible) still use techniques that may require consent, and skepticism that first-party analytics cookies qualify as 'strictly necessary.'
selected_brief.mechanism: Simple Analytics documents no cookies, no trackers and no personal-data processing. When evaluating a site, its onboarding scans the technology and supplies an appropriate installation option; the code still has to be added through the relevant site or platform route.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: This is a strong alternative for the narrower case where a client already uses GA4: an assisted comparison on the client's own site can inform a measurement decision without requiring an immediate switch.
alternative_arguments.argument_issue: The proposed buyer problem is not linked to the assigned evidence. Select another complete argument while preserving campaign intent and action constraints.
claim_conditions: Present this as a conditional option for sites already using GA4.
Keep the 30-day duration attached to the assisted proof of concept.
Do not imply that the comparison automatically identifies one definitive cause for a pageview difference.

Do not describe the assisted proof of concept as self-serve.
Do not assume the recipient or every client currently uses GA4.

The assigned evidence does not establish that this function resolves the proposed buyer problem. Inspecting its source or starting an account does not demonstrate that outcome, a completed integration, or a result for this recipient.
alternative_arguments.call_to_action: Book a demo to define the measurement question for a free 30-day proof of concept alongside GA4.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The assigned evidence does not establish that this function resolves the proposed buyer problem. Inspecting its source or starting an account does not demonstrate that outcome, a completed integration, or a result for this recipient.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Respect the campaign objective and name only a supported proposition; do not imply novelty without user-provided or dated support.

selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: privacy-friendly analytics is another label whose consent implications must be taken on trust. After: Simple Analytics documents the relevant mechanisms—no cookies, trackers or personal-data processing—and offers a site-specific installation path that can be evaluated on a suitable build.
must_not_say: Do not claim that Simple Analytics removes every legal or compliance obligation for every client, configuration or jurisdiction.
Do not claim that all privacy-friendly analytics tools use fingerprinting, cookies or personal data.
Do not promise that the same installation step works across every client site; onboarding is technology-dependent.
Do not claim a portfolio-wide price, unlimited client domains or favorable agency economics.
Do not imply guaranteed time savings, easier maintenance, higher traffic counts or better business results.
Do not introduce GA4 comparisons, pageview-gap claims, security infrastructure, encryption, scroll depth, page-view duration or AI-assistant data routing into the primary argument.
Do not assume the reader has permission to deploy on a client website.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
selected_brief.objection: Does cookie-free actually mean this analytics option avoids the identifiers and personal-data processing behind the consent concern?
selected_brief.tone: Matter-of-fact, specific and reassuring; lead with the product design and its practical consequence without urgency or legalistic language.
selected_brief.call_to_action: Start for free and review the installation option for one representative website.

selected_brief.next_step_limit: Reviewing onboarding does not establish portfolio-wide compatibility, total agency cost, client approval or the legal requirements of every client and jurisdiction; actual analytics behavior requires installation on a permitted site.
selected_brief.subject_strategy: Surface the concrete evaluation criterion—analytics without cookies, trackers or personal-data processing—rather than using a generic privacy promise or compliance guarantee.

brief.reader:
Selected audience: Agency or freelance developer choosing the analytics stack for client sites.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (inferred; check applicability): The corpus contains public developer discussion (two Hacker News threads) about whether websites need cookie consent banners and about named analytics tools (Google Analytics, Fathom, Plausible, SimpleAnalytics), but no quote in either thread identifies the speaker as an agency or freelance developer building or maintaining multiple client websites, or as selecting an analytics default on behalf of clients. The audience's defining workflow (choosing a repeatable analytics default across client builds to avoid consent-banner/DPA friction) is not directly evidenced here; only general developer debate about consent and analytics tool choice is present.
brief.reader_segment: Agency or freelance developer choosing the analytics stack for client sites
brief.promise: Simple Analytics gives developers a documented way to provide useful website analytics without cookies, trackers or personal-data processing, with installation guidance adapted to each website's technology.
brief.orientation: Simple Analytics is a cookie-free website analytics option for agencies and freelance developers evaluating a repeatable default across client sites, with per-site installation and documented privacy conditions.
brief.arc: Move from skepticism about broad privacy-friendly claims to the specific product design behind Simple Analytics, then invite a scoped self-serve evaluation for one representative website.
brief.sequence_rationale: With only one email, the strongest argument is the defining operational benefit supported by the dossier: analytics that requires no cookies, trackers or visitor consent and does not process personal data. The brief answers the audience's documented skepticism with product behavior rather than a generic compliance label. Technology-dependent installation is attached as a condition of adopting that benefit, not treated as a separate reason to buy. The CTA is a scoped evaluation rather than a portfolio-wide commitment because client-site permissions, plan limits and aggregate agency economics are not established. The GA4 proof of concept is preserved as a complete alternative for the narrower situation where a client already uses GA4. The single thing that would most change this campaign is a readable copy of the unavailable Simple Analytics source page.

emails.selection_reason: The audience research shows developers disputing whether privacy-friendly analytics actually avoids consent requirements. The product's documented absence of cookies, trackers and personal-data processing directly addresses that decision and is more broadly relevant than assuming the reader currently uses GA4.

value_case.reader_benefit: For a suitable client website, the developer can provide website analytics without adding cookies or trackers or processing visitors' personal data, reducing the analytics-related consent and DPA questions created by those practices.
value_case.mechanism: Simple Analytics states that it uses no cookies or trackers, requires no visitor consent and does not process personal data. During onboarding, it scans the website's technology and provides a corresponding installation option.
decision_conditions: The no-DPA statement rests on Simple Analytics' documented absence of personal-data processing and its stated GDPR basis; it is not a universal legal opinion for every client or jurisdiction.
Installation is per website and depends on the technology detected.
Client permission and suitability must be established before deployment.

claim_conditions: Describe the privacy benefit as Simple Analytics' documented product behavior, not a universal legal guarantee.
Keep the evaluation scoped to a representative website rather than an entire client portfolio.
Installation instructions vary with the website's detected technology.
Add each website and use the technology-detected HTML code or another documented platform or framework installation option.

emails.belief_shift: Before: privacy-friendly analytics is another label whose consent implications must be taken on trust. After: Simple Analytics documents the relevant mechanisms—no cookies, trackers or personal-data processing—and offers a site-specific installation path that can be evaluated on a suitable build.
must_not_say: Do not claim that Simple Analytics removes every legal or compliance obligation for every client, configuration or jurisdiction.
Do not claim that all privacy-friendly analytics tools use fingerprinting, cookies or personal data.
Do not promise that the same installation step works across every client site; onboarding is technology-dependent.
Do not claim a portfolio-wide price, unlimited client domains or favorable agency economics.
Do not imply guaranteed time savings, easier maintenance, higher traffic counts or better business results.
Do not introduce GA4 comparisons, pageview-gap claims, security infrastructure, encryption, scroll depth, page-view duration or AI-assistant data routing into the primary argument.
Do not assume the reader has permission to deploy on a client website.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
emails.objection: Does cookie-free actually mean this analytics option avoids the identifiers and personal-data processing behind the consent concern?
emails.tone: Matter-of-fact, specific and reassuring; lead with the product design and its practical consequence without urgency or legalistic language.
emails.call_to_action: Start for free and review the installation option for one representative website.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Simple Analytics' privacy design and technology-specific installation path merit a permitted trial on a suitable client build.
emails.next_step_value: The self-serve path lets the reader enter onboarding for a website, where Simple Analytics scans its technology and provides a corresponding installation option.
emails.next_step_limit: Reviewing onboarding does not establish portfolio-wide compatibility, total agency cost, client approval or the legal requirements of every client and jurisdiction; actual analytics behavior requires installation on a permitted site.
emails.subject_strategy: Surface the concrete evaluation criterion—analytics without cookies, trackers or personal-data processing—rather than using a generic privacy promise or compliance guarantee.

brief.voice_notes: Use the company's short cause-and-effect rhythm. Say what the product does, then what that changes for a developer evaluating it. Avoid superlatives, urgency, competitor attacks and named-person sign-offs.

reasons: A licensed product bridge exists only for the qualified slice.
allowed_claims: Simple Analytics requires no cookies, no trackers, and no consent from visitors.
The Self-serve plan costs €20/month, estimated for about 100k monthly pageviews.
The Self-serve plan includes 1 user; each additional user costs +€20/month.
Simple Analytics offers a free 30-day proof of concept to test it on your own website, including help optimizing the setup for proxies and custom domains.
Website data is stored in the EU, with primary infrastructure in the Netherlands.
Data only goes to a provider outside the EU when the customer opts in to a feature that needs it, such as the AI assistant.
By default, Simple Analytics does not collect or store any data for visitors who have Do Not Track enabled.
Simple Analytics collects and stores how long a page is viewed, counting seconds only while the page is visible and not when it is hidden.
Simple Analytics collects and stores how far a visitor scrolls on a page, recorded in 5% increments.
All analytics data is processed in the Netherlands (EU-hosted).
No IP addresses are stored; they are discarded immediately.
Data is encrypted, and only Simple Analytics controls the decryption keys.
Simple Analytics is hosted on infrastructure from Worldstream and Leaseweb.
Simple Analytics does not process personal data, so a Data Processing Agreement is not required when using it.
Simple Analytics processes only Page URL, Referrer, UTM parameters, Time zone, and Device and browser type as its data scope.
The installation flow is technology-dependent: Simple Analytics scans each site and offers install code based on detected technologies rather than a single universal step.
Across Simple Analytics generally, additional websites/subdomains added to an account do not cost extra individually, but are capped by a plan-wide website limit.
